instructions: The day before, or at least 8 hours ahead: heat the oven to 350°F and grease an 8-inch round baking pan with 1 tsp of the butter.
In a bowl, whisk the egg, the egg yolk and half the sugar until slightly foamy. Set it aside.

In a medium pot, stir the milk with the rest of the sugar, 1/4 tsp of the cinnamon and the vanilla. Grate in the zest of the orange. Warm it over medium heat for about 4 minutes, until it's steamy. Don't let it boil.
Take the pot off the heat. Ladle half the hot milk into the egg mixture a spoonful at a time, whisking the whole time.
Pour the egg mixture back into the pot and set it over medium heat.
Whisk in the semolina slowly. Keep stirring until the cream thickens and starts to bubble. Once it bubbles hard, keep stirring for 1 minute.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in 1 tbsp of the butter until it melts.
Spread the cream evenly in the pan. Melt 2 tsp of the butter and brush it over the top.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until the top is deep golden. It will look jiggly in the middle and sets as it cools.
Let the pie cool in the pan for 45 minutes. Cover it and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight.
In the morning, cut the pie into 8 squares. Dust them with the last 1/4 tsp cinnamon and drizzle with the honey. Serve cold or after 15 minutes at room temperature.
Cover the leftover squares and refrigerate. They keep for up to 4 days.
advance_prep_notes: Bake the pie the day before and chill it at least 6 hours
method_notes: Real Greek Recipes (the lead) makes a crustless semolina custard from milk, eggs and sugar, thickened on the stove and then baked; it is scaled here to a 2 cup milk pie for an 8-inch pan. Souvlaki For The Soul and Mia Kouppa agree on the method but use cornstarch or more eggs and a hotter stove step. The 4 day fridge keep comes from the lead; none of the three says it freezes, so no freezer time is given. The smaller pie bakes in less time than the full size one.
